'''Yaron Silberberg''' ({{Langx|he|ירון זילברברג}}; 1951 – April 21, 2019) was an [[Israel|Israeli]] [[physicist]] at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] where he worked on [[nonlinear optics]], [[integrated optics]], optical [[soliton]]s, and optical communication technology and physics with ultrashort [[laser pulse]]s.

== Life ==
Silberberg studied physics at [[Tel Aviv University]], earning a bachelor's degree in 1972 and at the Weizmann Institute, where he earned a master's degree in applied physics in 1975 and a doctorate in 1984. In between, he did research with the Israeli army from 1975 to 1979. From 1985 to 1994 he worked at [[BELLCORE|Bellcore]] in [[Red Bank, New Jersey]]. At Bellcore he studied guided-wave optics, optical amplifiers, and soliton physics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 June 2004 |title=Yaron Silberberg |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37278102900 |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=[[IEEE]]}}</ref> In 1994 he became an associate professor at the Weizmann Institute and in 1999 was promoted to Professor in the Physics of Complex Systems Department. Silberberg headed this department from 1999 to 2002. From 2002 to 2008 he was Dean of Physics and from 2008 onward he headed the Crown Photonics Center at the Weizmann Institute.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Yaron Silberberg {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/obituaries/2019/yaron_silberberg/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

Silberberg was a member of the Israeli Academy of Sciences. He became a fellow of [[Optica (society)|Optica]] in 1991.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards ==

* 2013 [[Max Born Award]]<ref name=":0" />
* 2015 [[Weizmann Prize for Research in the Exact Sciences]]
* 2018 [[Rothschild Prize]] in Physical Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-07 |title=Prof. Yaron Silberberg - Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/awards-and-appointments/prof-yaron-silberberg-2 |access-date=2024-04-08 |website=Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries from the Weizmann Institute of Science |language=en}}</ref>
